what_its_for: Tasimelteon is used to treat Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder (Non-24), a condition where your internal body clock does not follow the normal 24-hour cycle. This causes your sleep and wake times to drift later and later over time. It is also used to treat nighttime sleep problems in Smith-Magenis Syndrome. This medicine works by acting on melatonin receptors in your brain to help reset your body clock.
how_to_take: Take tasimelteon by mouth at the same time every night, about 30 minutes before your bedtime. You can take it with or without food, but try to keep it consistent. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. If you are taking the liquid form (Hetlioz LQ), shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully using the dosing syringe provided. Do not use a regular kitchen spoon to measure the liquid.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 20 mg (one capsule or the prescribed amount of liquid) taken once nightly, about 30 minutes before bedtime. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed. For children with Smith-Magenis Syndrome, the dose is based on body weight and will be determined by your doctor.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at your usual bedtime the following night. Do not take two doses on the same night to make up for a missed one. Taking extra doses will not help you sleep better and may cause unwanted side effects.
storage: Store tasimelteon capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store the liquid form (Hetlioz LQ) at room temperature and use within 90 days of first opening the bottle. Keep all forms of this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking tasimelteon, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do any activity that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleep aids, anxiety medicines, or opioid pain relievers, unless your doctor has approved it. Do not smoke or take medicines that strongly affect liver enzymes (like rifampin or fluvoxamine) without telling your doctor, as these can change how tasimelteon works in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe allergic reactions (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing); unusual or complex sleep behaviors such as sleepwalking, sleep-driving, or doing activities while not fully awake; worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm; severe dizziness or confusion; or if your sleep problems do not improve or get worse after a few weeks of treatment. Always tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you are taking before starting tasimelteon.
when_it_works: Tasimelteon may not work right away. Because Non-24 is caused by a misaligned body clock, it may take weeks to months of nightly use before you notice a significant improvement in your sleep pattern. It is very important to take it every night at the same time and not to stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you do not notice results immediately. Consistency is key for this medicine to work properly.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to the drowsiness and dizziness caused by this medicine. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of tasimelteon during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose or consider a different treatment. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is generally needed, but tell your doctor about any kidney conditions. Children: Hetlioz LQ liquid is approved for use in children with Smith-Magenis Syndrome. Safety in children with Non-24 has not been fully established.
